(a) Let $M$ be the set of $2 \times 2$ matrices $\{I, A, B, C, D, E\}$ where $I$ is the identity matrix and the other matrices are:
$A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$; $B = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$; $C = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$; $D = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$; $E = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$.

(b) Let $S_3$ be the set of all permutations of the elements of the set $\{1, 2, 3\}$.
Two of the elements of $S_3$ are thus:
$p_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$; $p_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$.

Given that $S_3$ is a group under the operation of composition, write down the group table. (Again, use letters $p_i$ for the elements.) [8 marks]
(c) Explain what is meant by saying that two groups are isomorphic.

in which each number after 3 is unchanged, deduce that $S_n$ under the operation of composition is not abelian.

Prove that your result is true for any group. [8 marks]

(i) (a) State clearly the conditions for the integral test to be applied to the series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n$.
Apply the integral test to the series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n}{n^2+1}$.

Setting $p = \frac{1}{2}$, what does the comparison tell you about the convergence or divergence of the series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2+\sqrt{n}}$?

Find an expression for $x_{n+1}$ in terms of $x_n$ and so, by letting $n = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$, derive the Newton–Raphson iterative method for solving $f(x) = 0$.
(b) Show that when the result in (a) is applied to the equation $x^2 - c = 0$ it becomes
$x_{n+1} = \frac{1}{2}\left\{x_n + \frac{c}{x_n}\right\}$, $n = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$

for $n = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$

Hence show that for any $x_0 > 0$, the sequence of iterates converges to $\sqrt{c}$. [24 marks]
